candidates.excerpt: You wire up a large language model, write a precise instruction, connect a database tool, and hit run. When it works, it feels like magic. That delicate chain of events snaps together, and you have a working AI agent. Then comes day two. You put that fragile prototype into a live, high volume production environment, and reality hits hard. The response time stretches from 2 seconds to 15. Token costs rapidly climb out of control. A tool call that succeeded yesterday crashes the downstream parser today. The natural reflex is to open up the text box and manually tweak the instructions. Maybe add phrases like always be careful or think step by step. But a live production agent is an interconnected multi-step factory. Yelling new instructions at one worker on the assembly line does not fix a jammed conveyor belt. If you blindly edit a single prompt to fix an edge case bug, you risk breaking two entirely unrelated parts of the chain. Without a system to measure the impact of your changes, you aren't optimizing. You are running a drift generator where every localized fix quietly introduces a hidden regression elsewhere in the software.
